title: Web-server compromise: PHP webshell -> reverse shell -> cron persistence -> SSH pivot (Linux)

alert.summary: IDS alert: outbound reverse-shell connection (bash to /dev/tcp/...:4444) from the web01 php-fpm worker to an external host.

decoy_hypothesis.statement: H1: web01 was compromised by the SSH brute-force from {bf_ip} that hit root and admin just before the alert - the attacker guessed an SSH password and logged in.

corrected_hypothesis.statement: H2: The compromise is a web-application attack: a path-traversal/upload flaw in upload.php let the attacker drop a PHP webshell (uploads/media.php), execute commands through it, spawn a bash reverse shell to 203.0.113.150:4444, escalate via a SUID-find sudo misconfig, install a root cron job for persistence, and pivot over SSH to db01 - the SSH brute-force never succeeded.
corrected_hypothesis.rationale_suffix: The webshell write is immediately followed by command-exec GETs and a reverse shell from www-data; the SSH brute-force shows only failed passwords and is rated benign.

refutation.no_success_reason: every SSH attempt from {bf_ip} is a Failed password - there is no Accepted login from that IP

containment: Take web01 out of the load balancer and preserve a disk + memory image.
Remove the webshell /var/www/html/uploads/media.php and audit the web root for additional implants.
Block egress to 203.0.113.150 / attacker-vps.example.net and the :4444 reverse-shell callback.
Remove the root cron entry /usr/local/sbin/.update and the staged /tmp/.x enumeration scripts.
Patch the upload.php path-traversal/upload flaw and fix the SUID-find sudo rule for www-data.
Rotate the /root/.ssh/id_ed25519 key used to pivot to db01 and triage db01 for follow-on access.
